# All definitions

This page holds the full text of every live definition of [README.md](../README.md), sorted by ID.

<a id="d-01"></a>

## D-01: Zama protocol `[STABLE]`

> The Zama backend as a whole.

Aliases: protocol.

The Zama protocol is the Zama backend as a whole.

<a id="d-02"></a>

## D-02: Protocol generation `[EVOLVING]`

> One iteration of the Zama protocol, named today by its major and minor version numbers.

Aliases: generation.

A protocol generation is one iteration of the Zama protocol. Each new generation replaces the current one. Today, the major and minor version numbers name a generation, and every release of that generation shares them:

| Generation    | Releases |
| ------------- | -------- |
| protocol v13  | `0.13.x` |
| protocol v14  | `0.14.x` |
| protocol v1.0 | `1.0.x`  |

This definition describes the protocol as it works now. If the protocol design changes, what makes a new generation and how a generation is numbered can change too.

Internal text names a generation by its place, as in `<vN>` or `<vN-1>`, never by its number. [R-05](../../rules/entries/R-05.md) gives the notation.

<a id="d-03"></a>

## D-03: Protocol hotfix `[STABLE]`

> A fix to one protocol generation that leaves the generation unchanged.

Aliases: hotfix.

A protocol hotfix fixes one protocol generation. A hotfix changes only the patch number, so the generation stays the same. For example, `0.13.6` is a hotfix of protocol v13.

<a id="d-04"></a>

## D-04: Protocol version `[STABLE]`

> A name that usually means the protocol generation.

Aliases: version.

"Protocol version" usually means the protocol generation. To name one hotfix, write the full version number, such as `0.13.6`.

<a id="d-05"></a>

## D-05: Registered definition `[STABLE]`

> A definition that lives in the `entries/` folder of a definition folder and appears in its index.

A registered definition lives in a definition folder, as `entries/<ID>.md`, and appears in the index of that folder, its `README.md`. [The `reg-definitions` skill](../../../../.claude/skills/reg-definitions/SKILL.md) gives its format, and it passes `generate-index.mjs --check`.

A registered definition has an ID that never changes, aliases that the script checks, and one place where every reader finds it. It wins over every loose definition of the same term. [R-06](../../rules/entries/R-06.md) gives the rule.

<a id="d-06"></a>

## D-06: Loose definition `[STABLE]`

> A definition that explains a term only where the term is used, outside any definition folder.

A loose definition explains a term only where the term is used, for example in a sentence of a rule or in a code comment. It has no ID, and no script checks it.

Loose definitions are allowed. A loose definition never contradicts a registered definition of the same term. If the two disagree, the registered definition holds, and the loose one is the text to fix. To give a registered term another meaning, change its registered definition with the `reg-definitions` skill instead of redefining it locally. [R-06](../../rules/entries/R-06.md) gives the rule.

<a id="d-07"></a>

## D-07: Definition folder `[STABLE]`

> A registry folder, usually named `definitions/`, that holds registered definitions.

Aliases: definitions folder.

A definition folder is a registry folder whose `README.md` declares `kind: definitions`. Its `entries/` folder holds one file per registered definition, named `<ID>.md`, its `README.md` indexes them, and its `groups/` folder holds the generated group pages. For example, `global/definitions/` holds the global definitions, from `entries/D-01.md` on.

Every file in the `entries/` folder of a definition folder is a registered definition. [The `reg-definitions` skill](../../../../.claude/skills/reg-definitions/SKILL.md) gives the format of the files, and `generate-index.mjs` checks them.

<a id="d-08"></a>

## D-08: Rule folder `[STABLE]`

> A registry folder of the kind `rules`, usually named `rules/`, that holds one rule book.

Aliases: rules folder.

A rule folder is a registry folder whose `README.md` declares `kind: rules`. Its `entries/` folder holds one file per rule, named after the ID of the rule, its `README.md` indexes them, and its `groups/` folder holds the generated group pages. For example, `global/rules/` holds the global rules, from `entries/R-01.md` on.

[The `reg-rules` skill](../../../../.claude/skills/reg-rules/SKILL.md) gives the fields of a rule, and [the `reg` skill](../../../../.claude/skills/reg/SKILL.md) gives the layout and the script.

A rule book not converted yet keeps its rules in topic files, next to a `rules.md` that indexes them, as `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/rules/` does today.

<a id="d-09"></a>

## D-09: Definition tag `[STABLE]`

> The tag in the front matter of a registered definition that says whether the definition can change or is retired.

A definition tag sits in the `tag` field of the front matter of each registered definition. It says whether the definition can change, and whether the definition is still in use.

[`TAGS.json`](../../../../.claude/skills/reg-definitions/TAGS.json), in the folder of the `reg-definitions` skill, lists the definition tags and their meanings. It is the only list. Every generated index, such as [README.md](../README.md), shows it as a table.

A definition tag is not a rule tag. A rule tag says whether a rule and the code agree. Write "definition tag" or "rule tag" wherever "tag" alone could mean either.

<a id="d-10"></a>

## D-10: Rule tag `[STABLE]`

> The tag of a rule that says whether the rule text and the code agree.

Aliases: status tag.

A rule tag sits in the `tag` field of the front matter of each rule. It says whether the rule text is accurate, whether the code follows it, and whether a check enforces it.

[`TAGS.json`](../../../../.claude/skills/reg-rules/TAGS.json), in the folder of the `reg-rules` skill, lists the rule tags and their meanings. It is the only list.

A rule tag is not a definition tag. A definition tag says whether a definition can change or is retired. Write "definition tag" or "rule tag" wherever "tag" alone could mean either.

<a id="d-11"></a>

## D-11: Registry folder `[STABLE]`

> A folder that holds one kind of entry, such as definitions or rules, with a generated index, one file per entry, and generated group pages.

Aliases: registry.

A registry folder holds one kind of entry. Its layout is the same for every kind:

- `README.md`: the index. Its front matter names the kind and the ID prefix and declares any groups. The script `generate-index.mjs` of [the `reg` skill](../../../../.claude/skills/reg/SKILL.md) generates the part between its two markers.
- `entries/`: one file per entry, named after its ID, as in `entries/D-02.md`. The front matter of each file holds the data of the entry.
- `groups/`: the generated pages, one per group, and `all.md` with every live entry.

The kind sets the letter of the IDs, the fields of an entry, and the list of tags. A definition folder is a registry folder of the kind `definitions`.

<a id="d-12"></a>

## D-12: FHEVM group `[EVOLVING]`

> One deployment of the Zama protocol, with one gateway, one relayer, and one KMS, that serves one or more host chains.

Aliases: FHEVM chain group, FHEVM network.

An FHEVM group is one deployment of the Zama protocol. One gateway, one relayer, and one KMS serve the host contracts that the group deploys on each of its host chains ([D-13](../entries/D-13.md)). Every group has exactly one canonical chain ([D-14](../entries/D-14.md)).

Three groups exist today:

| Group     | Canonical chain             | Non-canonical chains                                            |
| --------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mainnet` | Ethereum Mainnet (1)        | Polygon (137)                                                   |
| `testnet` | Ethereum Sepolia (11155111) | Polygon Amoy (80002), BSC Testnet (97)                          |
| `devnet`  | Ethereum Sepolia (11155111) | Polygon Amoy (80002), BSC Testnet (97), Ethereum Hoodi (560048) |

In `fhevm-chains.config.json`, a group is an entry of `networks`, with its `relayerUrl` and its `gateway`.

The local stack is not an FHEVM group. It is the cleartext mock that a test deploys on a local chain, as on chain 31337. No gateway, relayer, or KMS serves it. The code calls it the `local` group, as the `fhevmGroup` field of forge-fhevm-std does, and so do some rules. That name does not make it an FHEVM group.

This definition describes the protocol as it works now. If the protocol design changes, what a group holds can change too. Groups can also be added or removed, so the table above can change.

<a id="d-13"></a>

## D-13: Host chain `[EVOLVING]`

> An EVM chain on which an FHEVM group deploys its host contracts.

Aliases: host.

A host chain is an EVM chain on which an FHEVM group deploys its host contracts, such as `ACL`, `FHEVMExecutor`, `KMSVerifier`, and `InputVerifier`. Not every host chain has every contract: only the canonical chain of a group has a `KMSGeneration`. D-14 and D-15 say which contracts the canonical and the non-canonical chains hold.

One host chain can host several groups, each with host contracts of its own at addresses of its own. Ethereum Sepolia hosts `testnet` and `devnet`, and so do Polygon Amoy and BSC Testnet. So a chain id names a host chain, but not a group: a text that means a group on Ethereum Sepolia names `testnet` or `devnet`.

In `fhevm-chains.config.json`, each entry of `networks.<group>.hosts` describes one host chain for one group, and its `id` is the chain id. The key of the entry is a name that the group gives the chain. Two groups can give one chain two names: chain 97 is `bsc_testnet` in `testnet` and `bnb_testnet` in `devnet`.

This definition describes the protocol as it works now. If the protocol design changes, the list of host contracts can change too.

<a id="d-14"></a>

## D-14: Canonical chain `[EVOLVING]`

> The one host chain that an FHEVM group designates among its host chains, so that each group has exactly one.

Aliases: canonical host chain, FHEVM canonical chain.

Each FHEVM group names one of its host chains as its canonical chain. A group has exactly one, so there are as many canonical chains as groups, counted per group:

| Group     | Canonical chain             |
| --------- | --------------------------- |
| `mainnet` | Ethereum Mainnet (1)        |
| `testnet` | Ethereum Sepolia (11155111) |
| `devnet`  | Ethereum Sepolia (11155111) |

Being canonical belongs to the pair of a group and a host chain, and not to the chain alone. Ethereum Sepolia is the canonical chain of `testnet` and also of `devnet`: two groups share one chain, and each names it canonical. Every other host chain of a group is a non-canonical chain ([D-15](../entries/D-15.md)).

The canonical chain holds the group's `KMSGeneration` and the group's `ProtocolConfig`:

- `KMSGeneration`: a group has one, on its canonical chain. No other host chain of the group has one.
- `ProtocolConfig`: the canonical chain holds the group's `ProtocolConfig`. Each non-canonical chain also has a `ProtocolConfig` of its own today.

Every canonical chain is an Ethereum chain today. That is a fact about the groups as they are, not a requirement.

This definition describes the protocol as it works now. A group can name another canonical chain, and a new group names its own.

<a id="d-15"></a>

## D-15: Non-canonical chain `[EVOLVING]`

> A host chain of an FHEVM group that is not the canonical chain of that group.

Aliases: non-canonical host chain.

A non-canonical chain is any host chain of an FHEVM group other than its canonical chain. Today:

| Group     | Non-canonical chains                                            |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mainnet` | Polygon (137)                                                   |
| `testnet` | Polygon Amoy (80002), BSC Testnet (97)                          |
| `devnet`  | Polygon Amoy (80002), BSC Testnet (97), Ethereum Hoodi (560048) |

A non-canonical chain has no `KMSGeneration`: the group has one, on its canonical chain. It has a `ProtocolConfig` of its own.

A group can have any number of non-canonical chains, none included.

This definition describes the protocol as it works now. A group can add or remove non-canonical chains.
